shortfall_reason: The 2.6 -> 2.9.1 window contains 17 candidate changes and only 13 of them carry a behavior difference that a public-API contract can observe, so the Pack ships 13 contracts (9 public + 4 heldout) instead of 16. The four held-out demands were kept at full strength because they carry the transfer measurement; the shortfall was taken entirely on the public side, which drops from 12 to 9. Four candidates were rejected for having no observable behavior difference at all (annotation-only typing changes, test-only accommodation for a stdlib parser change, the lazy-pattern-construction refactor and its two follow-ups, and two Python-version support-matrix changes). No demand was invented and no contract was weakened to reach a count.

rejected_candidates.reason: Documentation typo only; no code path changes.

Type-annotation corrections (return types widened to include None) plus a lint config tweak. Annotations do not change runtime behavior, and the runtime results the new annotations describe are already correct on the starter tree, so no starter-fails / reference-passes contract exists.
Support-matrix change (adds Python 3.14, drops 3.8) confined to CI workflows, packaging metadata and the version constant. Not observable from a frozen tree exercised on a single interpreter.

The changelog describes this as test-only accommodation for a stdlib HTML parser change. The library diff is a coverage pragma plus a no-op cast with a None guard on an internal language cache; no selection result changes between endpoints.
Documentation toolchain migration; no library code.
Build-backend version requirement bump; no library code.
Upstream test adjusted for Windows; no library code.

Lazy construction of parser patterns and regexes. The only effect is import cost (~26ms to ~5ms), which is not separable from interpreter startup, and every compile and select result is identical on both endpoints.
Follow-up refactor of the lazy pattern accessor; no observable difference beyond pr_296.

Follow-up rework of the lazy selector mapping, including locks around lazy compilation. The starter tree compiles eagerly and is therefore already thread-safe here, so there is no starter-side defect to contract against.
Support-matrix change (drops Python 3.9) confined to CI workflows, packaging metadata and the version constant.

Cosmetic follow-up to pr_298 that swaps one never-matching regex sentinel for another. Folded into hidden_empty_substring_attribute_match rather than given its own demand, because it produces no behavior difference of its own.

notes: pr_280 supplies three demands (`:open`, the recognized-only live-viewer states, and `:muted`) because it lands three independent selection behaviors; pr_288 supplies three (namespace key validation, the selector dump hang, and the ISO week limits) for the same reason.

Five contracts are termination contracts: the defect they encode is that the starter tree never returns, so the work runs in a child interpreter under a wall-clock budget. Each budget is at least two orders of magnitude above what the reference endpoint needs for the same input, so the assertion measures termination rather than speed.
